profile.summary: 3UTRBERT is an RNA language model for 3' untranslated regions (3'UTRs), the stretch of an mRNA after the coding sequence that carries many regulatory signals. It is a BERT model pre-trained on human 3'UTR sequences, read as overlapping k-mer tokens, and then fine-tuned to predict RNA-binding protein sites, m6A modification sites and where an mRNA sits in the cell. Its attention scores can be used to highlight regions with likely regulatory function.

summary_quotes.text: Here 3UTRBERT is described, which implements an attention‐based language model, i.e., Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT).

3UTRBERT is pre‐trained on aggregated 3'UTR sequences of human mRNAs in a task‐agnostic manner; the pre‐trained model is then fine‐tuned for specific downstream tasks such as identifying RBP binding sites, m6A RNA modification sites, and predicting RNA sub‐cellular localizations.
the self‐attention mechanism within 3UTRBERT allows direct visualization of the semantic relationship between sequence elements and effectively identifies regions with important regulatory potential

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: 3UTRBERT is the encoder part of a Transformer: token embeddings of dimension 768 plus positional embeddings pass through twelve stacked Transformer layers, each with multi-head self-attention and a feed-forward layer. Sequences are split into overlapping k-mer tokens. It was pre-trained as a masked language model: 15% of the k-mers are masked, in contiguous spans of k tokens so that a masked k-mer cannot be read off its neighbours, and the model learns to restore them; next sentence prediction was dropped. For downstream use, the model is either fine-tuned end to end on short labelled sequences, or frozen and used to extract embeddings for longer sequences.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Four pre-trained checkpoints are linked from the README, for 3-mer, 4-mer, 5-mer and 6-mer tokens. The paper says they share the same architecture and training settings. The 3-mer checkpoint is a single zip file of 322227069 bytes on figshare. Fine-tuning and prediction must use the tokenizer that matches the checkpoint (rna3 to rna6). A result should name the k-mer checkpoint, its figshare version, and the fine-tuning data.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Masked RNA language model (BERT) for 3'UTR sequences, fine-tuned for downstream tasks

quotes.text: to learn general‐purpose representations using a masked language model, i.e., reconstructing the masked tokens from other tokens

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer encoder (BERT): embedding dimension 768, twelve stacked Transformer layers with multi-head self-attention and position-wise feed-forward layers, 12 attention heads shown per layer.

quotes.text: = 768. And the positional embedding was then summed with token embedding as the final input of the Transformer encoder network.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: RNA sequences tokenised into k-mers (k = 3, 4, 5 or 6). For fine-tuning, a FASTA file with the label in each sequence ID, split by preprocess.py into train.tsv, dev.tsv and test.tsv. For feature extraction, a FASTA file named seq_to_extract.fasta.

quotes.text: The input file is in `.fasta` format. For each sequence, the label of the sequence should be in the sequence ID.
The input fasta file should be named as `seq_to_extract.fasta`.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Embeddings per base from the pre-trained model; from a fine-tuned model, per-sequence probabilities (pred_results.npy) and evaluation metrics (pred_results_scores.npy); attention maps, mutation heatmaps and motifs from the analysis scripts.

quotes.text: Pre‐trained on human 3'UTR sequences, it is fine‐tuned to identify RBP binding sites, m6A RNA modifications, and RNA sub‐cellular localizations.

run_guide.summary: Set up the conda environment, install the repository, download the pre-trained 3-mer checkpoint, fine-tune it briefly on the repository's 3-mer example data, and predict on the example test set.

notes: The existing source (Wang et al. 2026 zero-shot benchmark supplement) is a benchmark that evaluated 3UTRBERT. A Hugging Face model yangheng/3utrbert exists; its owner is not the 3UTRBERT authors' GitHub account, so it was not used and may be a third-party conversion. A fly variant repository (braselog/3UTRBERT_fly) also exists and is not covered. The first Europe PMC fetch of the paper returned an HTTP 500 page; the retry succeeded and that copy is the one saved. The paper's full text does not mention a GitHub repository; it links the figshare dataset (10.6084/m9.figshare.26082916.v1), which the README also links, so the repository is taken as official from that shared link and the README's content. The README's feature extraction script appears broken at the pinned commit (see limitations), so the run guide uses fine-tuning and prediction instead.
